capturedBy: A thread created over `codex app-server` under an isolated CODEX_HOME, then driven by a
real `codex resume` TUI and by `codex exec resume --skip-git-repo-check`. The index file
is that home's session_index.jsonl after three renames: one at creation, one from a
second app-server connection, one typed as `/rename` into the TUI.
turn-aborted.captured.jsonl is a single line lifted from local codex history — no probe
produced an interrupted turn, and the record carries no prose.
rollout-content.captured.jsonl is a second rollout, captured 2026-08-22 from three turns
under a throwaway CODEX_HOME, and NOT filtered to event_msg: it keeps the response_item
records the timeline mapper reads and rollout.captured.jsonl has none of. The plan's
recipe for it — a bare `codex exec` under an isolated CODEX_HOME — misses the production
shape twice over. An isolated home has no credentials, so auth.json was copied into it;
and a thread CREATED by `codex exec` (session_meta source "exec") writes an
item_completed event surface, where a thread created over `codex app-server` (source
"vscode", which is what CodexAdapter.prepare does) writes user_message/agent_message —
even for turns a different process drives later. So this was captured the way Flight Deck
runs: thread/start, thread/name/set and archive/unarchive over a real `codex app-server`,
then three turns driven by `codex exec resume --skip-git-repo-check` in a temp workdir.
The third turn calls a throwaway stdio MCP server (an echo tool, written for the capture)
to get an mcp_tool_call_end record. codex-cli 0.148.0 routes even that through its
unified `exec` custom_tool_call, and no invocation on this machine could make it write a
function_call at all — that shape is covered by CodexTimelineMapperTests from records in
the 494-rollout local corpus instead of by this capture.
editingRule: Lines may be DROPPED, never EDITED. rollout.captured.jsonl is the source rollout filtered
to `session_meta` and `event_msg` records. rollout-content.captured.jsonl is its own
source rollout with the fourth and last turn dropped, as a duplicate in shape of the
first. In both, every surviving line is byte-for-byte what codex wrote.
Unlike codex-app-server-v2.generated.json, this is not generated from a schema, because
no schema for these formats exists — `codex app-server generate-json-schema` covers the
protocol only. That makes these files the weakest ground truth in the suite: they record
what codex DID on one day, not what it DECLARES. `CodexIntegrationTests` is what notices
when that stops being true; run it with FLIGHT_DECK_CODEX_INTEGRATION=1.
Every fixture in this directory MUST be named *.captured.* to signal that it is verbatim
captured output, not authored. Tests must reference captures by their documented name; if
a test cannot find its fixture, correct the lookup name in the test, never add an undocumented
copy under another name. Undocumented copies hide the data source and can silently diverge from
the original when concurrent sessions commit. This rule prevents that category of bug.
